references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). LE: files/Attach_1_-_Blood_Transfusion_Services_SOW.pdf ===== Statement of Work For Transfusion Services 20 October 2026 I. Background: The 88th Medical Group Transfusion Services requires blood components and references lab transfusion testing services. The supplier shall provide blood products and reference blood transfusion services (testing) to support the blood supply in case of emergency situations and inpatient and outpatient care at the WPAFB Medical Center when requested for a period of 5 years at the prices in the approved price list. II. Minimum Technical Requirements: The supplier shall provide blood products and reference transfusion testing that are time dependent with immediate response and expedience to treat critical patients. The supplier must operate 24/7 as the 88th Medical Group (MDG) is a 24/7 operation; this service must be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays and weekends. The supplier shall provide rapid shipment of blood products when the 88 MDG Transfusion Services in-house inventory is in need to support critical patients. The one-hour turnaround time for testing is a mission-critical requirement. The blood supplier shall deliver routine blood products ordered on a STAT basis within one (1) hour of the blood sup

eipt of an emergent request for blood products. The required completion point is delivery to the Transfusion Services department. The supplier must fulfill our request with the ordered product with appropriate compatible blood type, applicable testing, and requested quantities. Any unforeseen delays are understandable; however, the ultimate goal is for the delivering agency to aim for the <1 hour delivery time. An appropriate transmittal list is required with each delivery. If emergent requests are unable to be consistently met, it could mean critical failure for our hospital's life-saving capabilities. The supplier shall have 24/7 reference laboratory testing capabilities for patients anticipating transfusions or medical treatment. The supplier must be licensed by the Food & Drug Administration (FDA) and follow American Association of Blood Bank (AABB) standards. The supplier must notify the 88th MDG Transfusion Services of all unexpected/abnormal tests from blood products supplied by them. The supplier shall provide look-back notifications to the 88th MDG as required by 21 CFR 610.48 (b)(3): (a) within three (3) calendar days if blood collected from a donor who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV or HCV infection on a later do
